newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian rightists mull Visco no-confidence motion.
newsitem.headline: Italian rightists mull Visco no-confidence motion.

text.p: Italy's hard right National Alliance might table a parliamentary motion of no-confidence against Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco, party leader Gianfranco Fini said in a statement on Monday.

"We are considering the possibility of presenting an individual motion of no-confidence against Minister Visco," the statement said, adding that small businesses in Italy were "exasperated" by the government's fiscal policy.
Visco has pledged to reform Italy's complex fiscal system and has already unveiled plans to introduce a new regional tax (Irep) aimed at corporates and self-employed workers.

He has drawn heavy criticism from across the political spectrum for proposing to lift the minimum personal tax rate to 20 percent from the present 10 percent and reduce the top tax rate to 46 percent from 51 percent.

The government is also planning a one-off "Euro-Tax", which has yet to be outlined but which it is hoped will raise some 12.5 trillion lire next year. Visco has promised that the measures will not harm productive output but small businesses fear the worse.
